messages:
alex: FYI rolling CUDA 15.0 driver yesterday correlates with a perf hop on several text-gen routes. P95 up ~25% on long prompts (>256). profiler show kernel 'attn_fused_opt' falling back to 'attn_generic' for seqlen>256 :thinking_face:

maya: Ugh. Any sign it's kv-cache related or just kernel selection?

alex: KV cache hitrate looks stable. CPU+NVTX traces show the callsite picks a different kernel path at layer 14 when seq_len crosses 257. Here's a snippet from the profiler (condensed):
```
Profile dump: route=/v1/generate, model=rwkv-13b, batch=1
seq=256 -> attn_fused_opt (3.4ms per layer)
seq=288 -> attn_generic   (5.8ms per layer)  <-- hotflip at threshold
KV hitrate: 0.93 both cases
Kernel selection log: pick_autotuned_kernel(seq_len=288, arch=sm90) -> tie-break -> generic
```

sam: Interesting — tie-breaker changed. Could be the autotuner entropy after driver changed kernel timings. Any recent autotune reruns?

alex: We did an autotune sweep during the rollout, but it used the new driver timings. Looks like the heuristic now prefers generic for wider seqlen ranges. We have two quick paths: rollback driver rollout, or patch autotuner heuristics to bias the fused kernel for sm90 when seq distribution skewed.

li: For immediate mitigation can we lower the batch-path threshold so requests that used to pick generic are forced to the fused one? That might reduce throughput but restore latency SLO.
maya: Agreed. Also check continuous batching heuristics: longer sequences can cause KV cache misses if batching window grows. But alex said KV is fine.

alex: Created a tiny canary change to force kernel override for the affected model on canary fleet: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=attn_fused_opt` for model rwkv-13b on h100-sm90 canary nodes. Deploy bot reported success:

ops-bot: deploy 1995000150 -> env set REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE on fleet:eng-runtime-canary (15 nodes). Status: succeeded.

sam: Good. Any perf numbers from canary?
alex: Canary p95 back down to baseline within minutes. Quick numbers: p95 route=/v1/generate baseline 120ms, post-driver 150ms, canary override 118ms.
maya: Sounds like autotuner tie-breaker needs adjustment. We should add an explicit arch-aware bias term so sm90 favors fused variant for seqlen in [128,512].

li: Long-term we should also persist autotune results with driver-version metadata so we don't re-learn bad ties post-upgrade. Right now autotune rewrites metrics and forgets the previous settled policy.
sam: Agreed. Action list:
- rollback plan if kernel override can't be applied fleet-wide quickly (ops)
- immediate: propagate `REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE` to critical pools (alex/ops)
- medium: tweak autotuner heuristics to add arch+seqlen bias (eng-runtime)
- long: store autotune fingerprints keyed by driver version + model + arch (eng-ml + eng-runtime)

maya: I'm adding a config flag to enable "driver-pinned-autotune" so we can opt-out of re-running autotune during driver rollouts.

alex: Thanks. I'll monitor canary and start a fleet-wide rollout of the override if stable. If anyone sees errors from the override, ping me.

li: Also adding a small perf test to the driver-upgrade playbook: run 10k gen tokens with seq mix and assert p95 delta < 10%.

sam: Nice. One more note — add a smoketrap in tracing to capture kernel selection decisions (kernel name + reason) for every stray p95 spike. That will save future sleuthing time.

alex: Good call. I'll open a follow-up with the trace fields. Closing for now, will update when fleet-wide status changes. :thumbsup:
